name: Luxembourg
kernel_parts_used: Surcharge (fonds pour l'emploi: flatPct 7 % + above 2 % on the cote)
kernel_gaps: credits written locally: CIS/CIP/CII have a phase-in from a base (300 + 2,9 %), a flat part and a phase-out, rounded up to the cent; CISSM is monthly
social contributions monthly (two SSM levels in 2025, ceiling and dependence abattement per month): local
class 1a is the tarif on a transformed income with capped marginal rates: written as its own schedule and checked against the statute's formula
Out is whole euros: cents kept in detail fields
company side (IRC art. 174 bands + FE + ICC) in harness/scan_lu.py, not in the kernel's company.json entry

validation.notes: all tax and SSC lines exact; CTGG/THP -4,48 (OECD allocation familiale, F2)

validation.referee: ACD Formules du calcul automatisé 2025 (income, classes 1/1a/2)
validation.notes: cote and cote+majoration at every multiple of 50, 0-400 000
sequential, 1,5 s apart; barème and total incl. fonds pour l'emploi

validation.referee: ACD annual salary table (décompte annuel) vs statute assessment
validation.notes: not agreement statistics: table - statute in [-10, +15] EUR, mean ~0 (F4, convention)

headline: The Luxembourg model matches the ACD's own calculator and formula sheet exactly (24 390 cases) and the OECD on every tax line; class 1a is worth 2 484 euros at any income, married parents pay up to 1 155 more than unmarried ones, a spouse's 936th euro of wage brings 492 euros of refundable credits, and the CISSM taper stacks to 64-74 % between 36 000 and 43 400.
